[P2] Require coverage for non-numeric thresholds

Every threshold rejection fixture supplies a number (`-0.1`, `1.5`, or `NaN`). Removing `typeof value !== "number"` therefore leaves all assertions unchanged, while allowing values such as `"0.7"` and `null` through JavaScript's numeric coercion. This violates CONTRIBUTING rule 4. Return to the validation/test design under rule 8 and require factory-time rejection of non-numeric thresholds before retaining this branch.
